findings.reason: Independently opened both original tiles separately at original resolution and read frozen/current source and local hybrid/RT0 suppliers. The caption calls the marks schematic flux arrows, while labels u1/u2 also suggest field samples; neither interpretation makes the original directions correct. Original displacements (-0.16,-0.16) and (0.16,0.16) are tangent to x=y, with zero component along either interface normal. They therefore cannot indicate the stated nonzero normal flux. At the original blue tail (0.72,0.38), u1=(-0.14,0.19), and at its midpoint (0.64,0.30), u1=(-0.18,0.15). At the original red tail (0.28,0.62), u2=(-0.14,0.19), and at its midpoint (0.36,0.70), u2=(-0.18,0.15). Both true fields point up-left, disagreeing with the displayed directions. Being wholly inside cells is not itself a defect for field samples. The small original lambda placement is cramped, but I do not independently assert clipping or a hard lambda-overlap defect; label spacing was adjusted with the necessary arrow correction.

diagram_math_checks.details: The closed square has vertices (0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1) and diagonal from (0,0) to (1,1). The lower-right region is K1={0<y<x<1} and the upper-left region K2={0<x<y<1}; f=1 and f=-1 labels agree with the Statement. The diagonal is the only interior facet; lambda labels its multiplier from def-na-hybridized-rt0-darcy-system. The fresh crop visibly contains all four boundary edges plus the diagonal.

From the Statement, u1(x,y)=((x-1)/2,y/2) and u2(x,y)=(-x/2,(1-y)/2). Blue tail (0.78,0.35) lies in K1 and u1=(-0.11,0.175), so 0.8u1=(-0.088,0.14), exactly the displacement to (0.692,0.49). Red tail (0.35,0.68) lies in K2 and u2=(-0.175,0.16), so 0.8u2=(-0.14,0.128), exactly the displacement to (0.21,0.808). Both segments stay in their convex cells. At blue midpoint (0.736,0.42), u1=(-0.132,0.21), still positively parallel to its arrow. At red midpoint (0.28,0.744), u2=(-0.14,0.128), also positively parallel.

K1 is below x=y, hence n1=(-1,1)/sqrt(2); K2 is above it, hence n2=(1,-1)/sqrt(2). For (s,s) on the diagonal, u1 dot n1=1/(2sqrt(2)) and u2 dot n2=-1/(2sqrt(2)). Multiplying by facet length sqrt(2) gives +1/2 and -1/2, matching Proof 1.1 and 2.1 and the outward-normal local/jump convention of def-na-hybridized-rt0-darcy-system. The two outward fluxes sum to zero, as required; no opposite physical flow direction is inferred from the negative second outward flux.

The Statement, hypotheses, Facts, complete numbered proof, dependencies, metadata and published status are byte-identical to the frozen before source. The diagram illustrates existing formulas and is outside the proof; Proof 1.1-3.1 remains a complete algebraic/integral argument independent of it.
